comparisons.peer_summary: The metrics include structured notes and liabilities with specific values provided for the years 2024, 2023, and 2022.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America report on structured notes as part of their funding or liability metrics in 2024, but they differ in specificity and intent. JPMorgan explicitly attributes the increase in structured notes to net issuances driven by client demand in its Markets segment, highlighting the active management of this funding source. In contrast, Bank of America provides a static snapshot of the magnitude of structured notes and liabilities ($48.4 billion) without attributing the change to specific business drivers like client demand or segment performance in the cited text. JPM focuses on the operational driver (client demand), while BAC focuses on the composition metric.
